payload.headline: Stocks bounce, but trend, fear and breadth still say stand aside

summary.thesis: SPY rose 1.62% and QQQ 2.69% on Nov 27, but both remain in downtrends below their 50- and 200-day averages. Fear is still 'elevated' and only 8% of stocks are above their 50-day averages.
summary.decision: Stand aside for both long-term buying and swing setups. The market gate stays active until QQQ closes above 682.74.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 682.74 (its 200-day average and the market gate) would end the tech downtrend. A QQQ close below 608.45 or SPY below 689.81 would set new 1-month lows, meaning the decline would be continuing.

payload.happening: Stocks had a strong day on Nov 27. SPY closed at 728.32, up from 716.70 (+1.62%), and QQQ closed at 650.99, up from 633.93 (+2.69%). Over five days SPY is up 1.74% and QQQ up 0.92%. Over 20 days both are still down, SPY by 5.33% and QQQ by 9.0%. Both bounced off 1-month lows set on Nov 20 (SPY 689.81, QQQ 608.45). Both remain well under their Oct 29 1-month highs (SPY 769.36, QQQ 715.34) and their past-year highest closes on Oct 6 (SPY 779.09, QQQ 759.66). No news was recorded since the last note. The next scheduled event is the jobs report (Employment Situation) on Dec 4 at 08:30, which shapes rate expectations.
payload.business: Trend: both indices are below their 50- and 200-day averages, which DATA classifies as a downtrend. SPY is close to its long-term line, 0.4% below its 200-day average of 730.98. QQQ is further away, 4.9% below its 200-day average of 682.74. Fear: the VIX was 26.8 on Nov 26, down from 28.29. That is still in the 'elevated' band (20–30) and at the 96th percentile of its last 252 readings, near the top of its one-year range of 13.47 to 35.89. This reading is stale: the Nov 27 VIX isn't stored yet, so today's rally is not reflected in it. Breadth: only 8% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, so very few stocks are in short-term uptrends. Read together, the bounce is real but narrow so far. Prices rose for a day, while the underlying trend, fear and participation readings still describe a market under stress. The recovery is not yet confirmed.

worth.text: No valuation is implied for the indices. The levels in this note are price-trend markers only.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: Both indices rallied on Nov 27 (SPY +1.62%, QQQ +2.69%) and are up over five days, holding above their Nov 20 1-month lows.
SPY is only 0.4% below its 200-day average of 730.98. A close above it would put the broad market's long-term trend back up.
The VIX eased from 28.29 to 26.8, and its five-day change is -1.64, so fear has stepped back from its recent level.
bear: Both SPY and QQQ remain below their 50- and 200-day averages, and DATA labels both trends 'downtrend'.
Breadth is 8%: very few stocks are in short-term uptrends, so the rally is not broad-based.
The VIX is still 'elevated' at the 96th percentile of its past 252 readings, and the latest stored value predates today's move.

longterm.why: QQQ closed at 650.99, 4.9% below its 200-day gate of 682.74. Fear is 'elevated' at 26.8 (as of Nov 26) and breadth is 8%. Today's bounce narrowed the gap, but trend, fear and breadth together still argue against new buying until QQQ closes above 682.74.

swing.why: QQQ is 8.4% below its 50-day average of 705.72. Below that level, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check. The 2.69% gain on Nov 27 moved QQQ closer but did not clear it.

decision.timing: The next scheduled event is the jobs report (Employment Situation) on Dec 4 at 08:30, which shapes rate expectations. The nearest levels are SPY 730.98 above and 689.81 below, and QQQ 682.74 above and 608.45 below. The 50- and 200-day averages move every day, while the 1-month highs and lows are fixed past prices. The Nov 27 VIX reading is not yet stored, so the fear read may update.

change_mind: A QQQ close above 682.74 (its 200-day average and the market gate) would end the tech downtrend. Together with a SPY close above 730.98, this would support moving from stand aside to selective.
A QQQ close below 608.45 or a SPY close below 689.81 would set new 1-month lows, meaning the decline would be continuing and reinforcing the stand-aside stance.
payload.what_changed: Since the Nov 25 note, QQQ rose from 633.93 to 650.99 and is now 4.9% below its 200-day gate, versus 7.7% before. The VIX eased from 28.29 to 26.8 (Nov 26) but stays 'elevated', and breadth is unchanged at 8%. The moving-average levels updated: QQQ's 200-day is now 682.74 (was 682.54) and its 50-day 705.72 (was 707.02). SPY's 200-day is now 730.98 (was 730.77) and its 50-day 757.2 (was 757.85). The 1-month highs moved to Oct 29: QQQ 715.34 and SPY 769.36. The decision is unchanged: stand aside. This is research, not advice.
